summary: Implement a FIFO queue using only stack operations.
mainInsight: Use two stacks: push onto an input stack; when the output stack is empty, pour the input stack into it (reversing the order). Each element moves at most once, so operations are amortised O(1).

approaches.name: Costly push
approaches.summary: Move everything between stacks on each push.

approaches.name: Two stacks with lazy transfer
approaches.summary: Transfer only when the output stack is empty.

promptVariants: How do two stacks implement a queue in amortised O(1)?
When should elements be moved between the stacks?
options: Move from the input stack only when the output stack is empty
Move from the input stack to the output stack on every push
Move from the input stack to the output stack on every peek
Never move elements; keep both stacks separate and search them
cards.answer: Move from the input stack only when the output stack is empty
cards.explanation: Elements keep their relative reversed order in the output stack and each moves once.

incorrectOptionExplanations.Move from the input stack to the output: Wasteful and can reverse order again.

promptVariants: Why does transferring reverse the order, and why is it amortised O(1)?
cards.answer: Popping from one stack and pushing onto another reverses the order, turning LIFO into FIFO for the transferred elements. Each element is pushed/popped on each stack at most once, so the total transfer work is O(n) over n operations: amortised O(1) per operation.
keyPoints: Each element moves at most once
cards.explanation: The cost of a transfer is paid by the pushes that created the elements.

promptVariants: Complete the statement: Amortised time per operation: ___
cards.explanation: Each element is moved at most once between the stacks.

promptVariants: What is the space complexity and the worst-case time for a single pop?
What is the worst-case cost of a single pop in the two-stack queue and its overall space?
cards.answer: O(n) total storage. A single pop can take O(n) when the output stack is empty and many elements must be transferred, but that cost is amortised.

promptVariants: Why transfer only `if not self.popStack`, and what bug appears if you transfer on every pop?
Why must elements only be moved when the output stack is empty?
cards.answer: If popStack still has elements, its top is the oldest remaining element (the queue front). Transferring then would put newer elements on top of older ones and break FIFO order. Only an empty popStack can safely receive the next batch.

promptVariants: After push(1), push(2), pop(), push(3), pop(), what is returned by each pop?
What order do the pops return?
cards.explanation: FIFO: 1 first. 3 is pushed after the first pop, so the next pop returns 2.
